name: John Ruskin
role: English art critic and social thinker (1819-1900)
summary: Ruskin called himself a violent Tory of the old school and an illiberal, yet also a communist of the old school. He rejected competition and laissez-faire economics, proposing government schools and workshops, fixed wages and state pensions, while opposing equality, universal equal suffrage and liberty as a goal, and favouring kings, hierarchy and obedience to the wise. He held that war and empire can build national virtue, that women and men have complementary roles, and he deplored railways, factories and the division of labour.

notes: Sources: his own books and letters (Gutenberg texts of Unto This Last, Crown of Wild Olive with Munera Pulveris, Time and Tide, Fors Clavigera vols 1-5, Sesame and Lilies, Lectures on Art, Stones of Venice) plus the 1911 Britannica. Themes searched without finding a stated position: healthcare, taxation, unions as such, immigration, race, abortion, sexuality, drugs, nuclear power, climate. His views shifted little from Unto This Last (1860-62) to Fors Clavigera (1871-84); from 1876 he attacked interest and rent in earnest (s12), but his earlier note on usury already leaned the same way. The Fors Clavigera volumes after vol. 5 were not read in full.
